report.source_text: After returning from the CT scan, the patient’s condition deteriorated within minutes. The oxygen saturation dropped to about 70% and did not recover even with 10 L of O2 administered via reservoir mask. Respiratory exhaustion was imminent. While intravenous Solu-Medrol and Co-Amoxicillin were administered, intubation was initiated, which proved to be extremely difficult due to swelling of the supraglottic soft tissue, although video-guided GlideScope was used. Consequently, the patient went into hypoxaemia and eventually into cardiac arrest. Reanimation protocol was immediately initiated. After even direct tracheal airway access failed, another attempt was made to orally intubate the patient, this time with success. After around 5 min of mechanical reanimation and a total of 2 mg intravenous adrenalin, ROSC was achieved.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 78-year-old woman with hypertensive cardiomyopathy presented with a 5-day progressive history of throat pain, hoarseness, painful submandibular swelling, dysphagia, coughing, and breathing difficulties. Initial vital signs showed fever (37.7°C), tachycardia (118/min), and hypertension (150/80 mm Hg). Laboratory studies revealed leucocytosis (17.2 g/L) and elevated CRP (125 mg/L). Physical examination demonstrated restricted mouth opening limiting direct visualization; meningism was ruled out. CT neck with IV contrast performed on admission revealed the thumbprint sign typical of acute epiglottitis with extensive supraglottic and subglottic swelling resulting in airway stenosis. Blood cultures obtained during hospitalization confirmed N. meningitidis bacteraemia. After returning from CT, the patient's condition rapidly deteriorated with oxygen saturation dropping to 70% despite high-flow oxygen. Intubation was initiated with intravenous Solu-Medrol and Co-Amoxicillin; initial attempts were extremely difficult due to supraglottic swelling despite video-guided GlideScope use. The patient developed hypoxemia and cardiac arrest requiring resuscitation. After failed direct tracheal airway access, successful oral intubation was achieved. Return of spontaneous circulation (ROSC) was achieved after approximately 5 minutes of mechanical reanimation and 2 mg intravenous adrenaline. Mechanical ventilation was continued for 11 days, after which the patient was weaned and tracheostomy was reversed. She was discharged to a neurorehabilitation facility to address neurological impairments from the hypoxic event.
